arguments.content: The challenge in clustered personalized federated learning lies in effectively balancing personalization and generalization across heterogeneous user clusters. This requires sophisticated algorithms to handle diverse data distributions while ensuring differential privacy guarantees. Additionally, maintaining privacy budget accounting over multiple rounds of client fine-tuning poses significant technical difficulties, given the risk of privacy budget reuse and cumulative privacy loss.

arguments.content: The key research gap addressed by this proposal is the lack of algorithms for clustered personalized federated learning that effectively incorporate differential privacy guarantees while adapting to heterogeneous and evolving user clusters. Existing works either focus on global models or fully personalized models but often overlook clustered structures that reflect real-world user groupings. Furthermore, methods to prevent privacy budget reuse during client fine-tuning rounds are underexplored, hindering practical deployment in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

arguments.content: The approach will develop novel algorithms for clustered personalized federated learning with integrated differential privacy guarantees. We will investigate adaptive clustering techniques that dynamically update user groups based on data distribution shifts. A key innovation is incorporating lightweight on-device calibration (building on our unpublished work UA-TOM-04) to improve model reliability while preserving privacy. We will also analyze client churn failure modes under rapid churn conditions, informed by our qualitative findings in UA-TOM-07, to design resilient federated learning protocols. The research includes rigorous empirical validation on real-world datasets and privacy auditing to ensure practicality and compliance.
